chapter: Kenton, Granz, Parker and the jazz clubs
title: Did Parker care about Afro-Cuban music?
summary: He says Parker was friendly and sounded natural with it.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah. Some of the jazz critics who don't know, you know, who are not frankly into Afro-Cuban music

have suggested that Parker basically played Afro-Cuban music because he was told to because he was under contract to GRANZ Brown, that unlike Gillespie, who always wanted to do it, but Parker was not particularly interested. What is your view on that, because you worked with him?

Well, he didn't give that impression to me, because the way he played -- the way he played is there. Anybody with sense and listen to the man play, some of (inaudible) just like you (inaudible) in your house and you in home.
Well, did you talk to him about African --
All the time. We were so friendly, every time he see us (inaudible). it was like seeing God.
Yeah. Can you tell -- I mean, can you remember any comments he made about playing (inaudible)?
Well, he never give me the wrong complaint or nothing, because everything was -- he was the type of guy, he never took much. Whatever (inaudible) with his saxophone.
